title: Plumber Salary Guide: Hourly Rates, Annual Pay, and Award Conditions
description: Learn how to calculate a plumber salary from hourly rates under the Plumbing Award. Includes casual loading, super, tax, and Fair Work Ombudsman classifications.
salarySummary: A full-time plumber under the Plumbing and Fire Sprinklers Award earns between $29.19 and $33.77 per hour (as at July 2024), which equates to $57,700 to $66,700 per year for 38 hours per week, before casual loading, super, and tax.

faqs.q: What is the average plumber salary in Australia?
faqs.a: The average plumber salary depends on experience, location, and employment type. According to the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) Average Weekly Earnings for May 2026, full-time adult ordinary time earnings were $2,083.70 per week, or about $108,352 per year. However, plumbers covered by the Plumbing and Fire Sprinklers Award earn award rates that range from $26.67 per hour for an entry-level worker to $33.77 per hour for an advanced tradesperson (as at July 2024). Many plumbers earn above award rates, so actual salaries can be higher. Use our [reference tables](/data) to compare classifications.

faqs.q: How is casual loading calculated for plumbers?
faqs.a: Casual plumbers receive a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate. For example, if a tradesperson level 1 has a base rate of $29.19 per hour, the casual rate is $29.19 × 1.25 = $36.49 per hour. This loading compensates for entitlements casuals do not receive, such as paid leave. The [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page explains how to apply it in the timesheet calculator.

faqs.q: What superannuation contributions are required for plumbers?
faqs.a: Employers must pay superannuation guarantee contributions of 12% of ordinary earnings on top of the plumber's base pay, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year (2026–27). For a full-time plumber earning $60,000 per year, the employer adds $7,200 in super. The [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page details how super is calculated and capped.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the plumber salary

A plumber salary in Australia is not a single figure. It depends on the classification under the **Plumbing and Fire Sprinklers Award 2020**, the type of employment (full-time, part-time, or casual), and any allowances or penalty rates. This guide explains how to convert an hourly rate to annual pay, what the award says, and how to use our [timesheet](/about) to estimate your take-home pay.

### How annual pay is calculated

The standard formula used on this site is:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

For full-time plumbers, ordinary hours are 38 per week under the award. So a plumber earning $30 per hour would have an annual gross of $30 × 38 × 52 = $59,280 per year. This assumes the same rate every week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, allowances, or salary sacrifice. The [hourly conversion](/blog). Higher classifications include:

- Tradesperson level 2: $1,141.57 per week ($30.04 per hour)
- Special class level 1: $1,173.97 per week ($30.89 per hour)
- Advanced tradesperson level 2: $1,260.37 per week ($33.17 per hour)

These rates already include industry and special allowances. Note that award rates change from 1 July each year. The Fair Work Ombudsman’s [pay guides](/blog) provide the latest figures.

### National Minimum Wage vs award rates

The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. Award rates for plumbers are higher, reflecting the skill and trade qualifications. Casual plumbers receive an additional 25% loading on top of the base rate. For example, a casual tradesperson level 1 would earn $29.19 × 1.25 = $36.49 per hour.

## Casual loading and superannuation

### Casual loading

If you work as a casual plumber, your employer must pay a 25% loading on the base hourly rate. This is in lieu of paid leave and other entitlements. Our [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page explains how to apply it in the calculator. Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading; instead, check the box in the timesheet to add it on top.

### Superannuation

Employers must contribute superannuation guarantee at 12% of ordinary earnings (from 1 July 2026). This is paid on top of your salary. For a full-time plumber earning $60,000 per year, the employer adds $7,200 in super. The maximum contribution base is $270,830 per year. Super is not deducted from your pay; it is an additional cost to the employer. See [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) for more.

## Tax and take-home pay

Your take-home pay depends on your total taxable income. The 2026–27 resident tax rates are:

- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus a Medicare levy of 2% (with reductions for low-income earners). The calculator on this site uses these rates and the full tax-free threshold. It does not deduct HELP repayments, the Medicare levy surcharge, or salary sacrifice. Use the [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page to understand the estimate.

## Using the timesheet calculator

Our [timesheet](/) lets you enter your base hourly rate. If you are casual, tick the box to add 25% loading. The calculator then shows:

- Annual gross (hourly × 38 × 52)
- Fortnightly and weekly gross
- Estimated tax and Medicare
- Estimated super (12% on top)

Remember that the result is an estimate. Actual pay may differ due to overtime, allowances, or different hours. Always check your pay against the award and your employment contract.

### Example: full-time tradesperson level 1

- Base rate: $29.19 per hour
- Annual gross: $29.19 × 38 × 52 = $57,679.44
- Fortnightly gross: $29.19 × 38 × 2 = $2,218.44
- Estimated tax (2026–27): about $8,400 (including Medicare)
- Estimated super: $57,679.44 × 12% = $6,921.53 (paid on top)

This example uses the award rate from July 2024. Current rates may be higher.

## Summary

A plumber salary can be estimated from the hourly rate using the standard formula. Award rates provide a minimum, but many plumbers earn above that. Casual loading and super are additional. Use our tools to convert your rate and see your estimated annual, fortnightly, and take-home pay.
